sections.reason: Title block, Status of This Memo, copyright notice, Abstract and Table of Contents. The Abstract states scope and binds nobody.

Introduction. Explains why AS_SET and AS_CONFED_SET complicate BGP security and states the document updates RFC 4271 and RFC 5065 and obsoletes RFC 6472. No RFC 2119 keyword; the obligations are stated in section 3.
Requirements Language boilerplate citing BCP 14. It defines keywords and obliges nobody.

The two obligations of the document, both mapped: 3:1 to RFC9774-3-1 (send) and 3:2 to RFC9774-3-2 (receive). The closing paragraph records which sections of RFC 4271 and RFC 5065 are updated and binds nothing further.
Describes how RPKI-ROV, BGPsec and ASPA already treat a route with an AS_SET. Descriptive, no RFC 2119 keyword, and it obliges no BGP speaker beyond the documents it cites.
Describes brief aggregation. Its one SHOULD is a quotation of RFC 4271 Section 5.1.6 and belongs to RFC 4271; the section adds no obligation of its own.
Explains why brief aggregation yields an unpredictable origin AS for RPKI-ROV. Descriptive, no RFC 2119 keyword.

Consistent brief aggregation. Its MUST (5.2:1) and its SHOULD to attach ATOMIC_AGGREGATE bind an aggregating implementation; Ze implements no aggregation, so 5.2:1 is excluded as feature-out-of-scope.
Section preamble: operator advice on deployment and configuration. No keyword.
Its MUST (6.1:1) binds an operator that aggregates; excluded as feature-out-of-scope with 5.2:1.
SHOULD NOT and SHOULD on announcing an aggregate to contributing ASes; recommendations conditional on aggregation, which Ze does not implement. No MUST-level site.
Reminds that RFC 4632 Section 5.1 Rule 2 binds aggregating implementations; it restates another document and adds no keyword.
Security Considerations. Notes the deprecation shrinks the attack surface. No keyword.
IANA Considerations: marks segment types 1 and 4 deprecated in the registry. A registry action, no speaker obligation.
References heading.
Normative references.
Informative references.
Example filtering policy for not advertising an aggregate to contributing ASes. Illustrative, no keyword.
Examples of consistent brief aggregation and the ROAs they need. Illustrative, no keyword.
Worked example of Appendix B. Illustrative.
Worked example of Appendix B. Illustrative.
Worked example of Appendix B. Illustrative.
Worked example of Appendix B. Illustrative.
Discussion of forwarding loops and AS_SETs. Explanatory, no keyword.

sites.quote: * MUST NOT advertise BGP UPDATE messages containing AS_SETs or AS_CONFED_SETs and
* MUST use the "treat-as-withdraw" error handling behavior per [RFC7606] upon reception of BGP UPDATE messages containing AS_SETs or AS_CONFED_SETs in the AS_PATH or AS4_PATH [RFC6793].

To ensure a consistent BGP origin AS is announced for aggregate BGP routes for implementations of "brief" BGP aggregation, the implementation MUST be configured to truncate the AS_PATH after the right-most instance of the desired origin AS for the aggregate.
sites.reason: Binds implementations of brief BGP aggregation only. RFC 4271 Section 9.1 makes route aggregation optional: "Route aggregation and information reduction can optionally be performed within this phase." Owner decision 2026-10-18 scoped this work to RFC 9774 and not to an aggregation feature (spec-bgp-rfc9774-as-set-deprecation, Key Design Decisions). Ze has no aggregation code: the AS_PATH parsers (ParseASPathText, internal/core/bgp/attribute/text.go) build only AS_SEQUENCE.

sites.quote: When aggregating prefixes, network operators MUST use consistent brief aggregation as described in Section 5.2.
